newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude bearish, supported at $19.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude bearish, supported at $19.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures were expected to weaken again on Friday although the market will find some support at $19.00-$19.05, technical analysts said.
August NYMEX crude oil closed unchanged on Thursday at $19.22 a barrel, while August heating oil was 0.55 cents down at 52.11 cents. Unleaded gasoline was 0.37 cents a gallon weaker at 58.60 cents.
"I would have to play this from the short side," said Hans Kashyap of the Analytics Research Corp. in Bethesda, Maryland.
He said he saw intraday resistance at $19.50, and then strong resistance above that at $19.75.
"That should pretty much contain prices for now," he said, adding that intraday support would weigh in first at $18.95-$19.00 and then at $18.50-$18.65.
Using his company's proprietary chart technique he saw a bearish scenario in the slightly longer term, with rallies up to $20.50 a barrel as opportunities to sell oil.
Gasoline, he said, was also looking negative, although the market seemed still to be trapped in a trading range between about 57.05 and 59.50-75 cents a gallon.
"We are in a trading range for now," he said.
"If we do go through 59.75 cents then we will be bound by 61.00-61.50 cents a gallon - it will be pretty stiff going up to there... ultimately I see a downside resolution to this."
He saw intraday resistance first at 59.25 cents and support at 57.75.
Brokers GNI in London were slightly more positive about gasoline.

Looking at the spot month continuation chart, they said in a daily report that an uptrend line drawn between the lows in late June and the low of July 7 was still significant, even though the price action pierced this line on Thursday.
"The dip below the uptrend line does not seem to have held in early ACCESS trade, therefore signalling that a test of the upper part of the range is in order."
The market stood at 58.80 cents a gallon shortly before the market opened, still just above this line.
The report cited resistance up at 59.60-59.80, dating from a series of lows formed early in April.
